newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast coffee bean exports rise in January.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast coffee bean exports rise in January.

text.p: Ivory Coast exported 5,373 tonnes of robusta coffee beans in January against 1,247 tonnes in December, but the cumulative 1996/97 total so far was still down on last season, official shipping data show.
Shipments included 4,594 tonnes of beans leaving from Abidjan, and 779 tonnes from San Pedro, the second port.
Coffee bean exports for January alone were up on a total of 4,147 tonnes shipped in January 1996.
Cumulative exports in the first four months of the 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) season were lower at 18,200 tonnes against 24,228 tonnes in the same period of 1995/96.
No roasted coffee was shipped but 861 tonnes of soluble coffee also left from Abidjan, against 498 tonnes in December -- and 278 tonnes in January 1995/96.

Coffee exports were slower in early 1996/97 than last year because of a combination of initially low world rates, bankers' caution over financing and longer grading time due to poor quality in some areas.
All of January 1995/96 exports were shipped from Abidjan.
Exporters expected shipment volumes to rise in February this year but data has not yet been compiled.
